requirement:
Habeas MUST locate its per-user configuration at
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/habeas/config.toml` on Unix when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is an absolute,
nonempty path, otherwise at `$HOME/.config/habeas/config.toml`. On Windows it MUST
use `%APPDATA%/habeas/config.toml`. `HOME` and `APPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. If no usable base directory can be
determined, an operation requiring user configuration MUST fail with an
explanatory diagnostic naming the variable.

The same user configuration MUST be usable across projects. Its location MUST
NOT be selected relative to the current project or changed by project settings.
User-local preferences for a project MAY remain in the user configuration;
workspace settings MUST use `habeas.toml` under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_location`.
rationale:
**Verdict:** the implementation covers every obligation in `user_location`, and the tests cover the interesting cases. No gaps found.

**Implementation**
- `user_config_path_from` (`src/config.rs` 618–631) builds the path as follows:
  - On Windows it uses `%APPDATA%` and appends `habeas/config.toml`.
  - On Unix it uses an absolute `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` when one is set.
  - Otherwise on Unix it uses an absolute `HOME` joined with `.config`, then appends `habeas/config.toml`.
- `absolute_directory` (654–660) accepts a variable only if it is set and `PathBuf::is_absolute()` is true. An empty value is never absolute, so empty and relative values are rejected together.
- `required_directory` (662–674) returns an `io::Error` with the message "cannot determine Habeas directory: {name} must be an absolute, nonempty path". The message names the variable (`HOME` or `APPDATA`), which is what the requirement asks for.
- The requirement says `HOME` and `APPDATA` must likewise be absolute and nonempty. `user_config_path_from` applies that rule to both. An invalid `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` falls back to `HOME`, as specified.
- `user_config_path` (613–616) uses `ConfigPlatform::current()` and the real environment. It takes no project argument and reads no project settings, so the location is never relative to the project or changed by project settings. A search of `src` found no other code that computes the user config path from `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `APPDATA`, `HOME` or `.config/`, so there is one implementation.
- `resolve_authoring` propagates the error with `?` before loading the user file, so the operation fails with the diagnostic. `is_configuration_file` in `src/redaction.rs` ignores the error, but redaction does not require user configuration.
- All the code involved carries `{impl}` markers: `ConfigPlatform`, `current`, `user_config_path`, `user_config_path_from`, `absolute_directory` and `required_directory`.
- The workspace-settings sentence is a `{cite}` of `workspace_location`. That requirement's text (nearest `habeas.toml`, no merging) is not the user-location rule, so it is correctly kept separate.

**Tests** (`tests/configuration.rs`)
- `locations_use_absolute_xdg_values_and_platform_fallbacks` (12–66) checks:
  - an absolute `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is used;
  - an empty or relative `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` falls back to `$HOME/.config/habeas/config.toml`;
  - Windows uses `APPDATA`;
  - an error occurs when no variables are set.
- `base_directories_must_be_absolute_and_nonempty` (1288–1328) checks:
  - an empty or relative `HOME` (Unix) or `APPDATA` (Windows) gives an error whose text contains the variable name;
  - a relative `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` falls back to an absolute `HOME`.
- These cover the boundaries (empty, relative, absolute, missing), the platform split, the fallback and the variable-naming diagnostic.
- Nothing tests project independence directly. That property follows from the function signature, which takes no project input, so I judged a test unnecessary.
- `ConfigPlatform::current` has no test, but it is a trivial `cfg!(windows)` switch.

text: :::{req} user_location
Habeas MUST locate its per-user configuration at
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/habeas/config.toml` on Unix when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is an absolute,
nonempty path, otherwise at `$HOME/.config/habeas/config.toml`. On Windows it MUST
use `%APPDATA%/habeas/config.toml`. `HOME` and `APPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. If no usable base directory can be
determined, an operation requiring user configuration MUST fail with an
explanatory diagnostic naming the variable.
The same user configuration MUST be usable across projects. Its location MUST
NOT be selected relative to the current project or changed by project settings.
User-local preferences for a project MAY remain in the user configuration;
workspace settings MUST use `habeas.toml` under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_location`.
:::{req} workspace_location
Habeas MUST search from its invocation directory upward for the nearest enclosing
`habeas.toml`. It MUST use that file alone, without merging ancestor workspace
files. A library operation given a project root MUST search from that root unless
its current directory is inside the project, in which case it MUST start there.
The directory containing the selected file defines the base for its relative
paths; it does not replace the Cargo and mdBook project root. A missing file MUST
mean absent workspace settings. Discovery MUST report unreadable candidate files
rather than silently selecting an ancestor. Loading MUST NOT create the file.
